transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, thank you for coming back to see me. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about the procedure we did on your arm yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong with the stitches?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The stitches are fine, but I need to talk to you about how the procedure actually went. I made a mistake while I was repairing the laceration.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: During the repair, I didn't check in with you enough to see if the numbing medicine was working. Because of that, I continued the procedure without making sure you had adequate anaesthetic infiltration. That means I performed the repair while you were still feeling pain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I did feel it. I thought... I thought perhaps it was supposed to be like that. I did not want to bother you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should never be like that. I am sorry that you had to experience that pain. I apologize. We were very busy in the emergency department yesterday, and I simply didn't focus on your pain levels the way I should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are the doctor. I trust you. Why are you telling me this now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is important that I am honest with you about your care. I can see that this is quite a shock to hear, and it feels very strange to have a doctor tell you they did something wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is very strange. In my home, we do not speak this way. The doctor is the authority. If you say it is okay, it is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you saying that. It shows a lot of trust in me, which makes me feel even more responsible for making sure I get this right. It must be distressing to feel like the trust was misplaced in that moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just felt... I felt I should be quiet. I did not want to be a difficult patient.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You were not being difficult at all. You were being patient, but you shouldn't have had to be. It was my job to ensure you were comfortable, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does this mean the arm is not healed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the injury itself is healing perfectly. The wound is closed and there is no lasting harm to your arm. The error was only in how the pain was managed during the stitching.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. So it is finished then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is finished, but I want to make sure we have a plan for your recovery so you feel supported. First, I want you to check the site for any new redness today. If you see anything, I want you to call the clinic immediately at this number.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am also going to schedule a follow-up appointment for you in exactly seven days. At that visit, I will personally check the wound before we remove the sutures.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Seven days. Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I also want you to know that I have documented this in my own performance file and discussed it with my supervisor. We are changing how we check for pain in the triage area to make sure this doesn't happen to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You would do that for a small thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It might seem small because there was no permanent injury, but your comfort and trust are not small things. I want to make sure I learn from this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I thank you for telling me. I am still surprised, but thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you for your kindness, Mrs. Al-Rashid. I will see you in a week.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a steady pace, and never interrupts or uses rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, but there were no explicit comprehension checks (e.g., 'Does that make sense?').

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am sorry', 'I apologize') and takes full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('shock', 'distressing') and references the patient's shared cultural context and feelings of being 'difficult'.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps (check for redness, follow-up in seven days), defines the patient's role (call the clinic), and addresses prevention (changing triage pain checks).
